prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CNC[C@@H](O)CCN1c2ccccc2N(c2ccccc2F)S1(=O)=O
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL222

Assay A:
  Description: Displacement of [3H]nisoxetine from human NET expressed in MDCK-Net6 cells
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: MDCK-Net6
  Test type: In vitro

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human NET expressed in MDCK-Net6 cells assessed as inhibition of norepinephrine uptake
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: MDCK-Net6
  Test type: In vitro

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.7, "error_class": "readout_type", "reason": "Assay A measures radioligand binding displacement (equilibrium binding affinity) while Assay B measures functional inhibition of norepinephrine uptake, and these two mechanistically distinct readouts often yield IC50 values that differ by more than 1.0 log unit, especially for compounds where binding affinity and transport inhibition potency are not tightly correlated."}
